source_text: In absoluto est igitur, si Moysi creditur magis, per quem Deus loquitur, quam Augustino, per quem Manichaeus, parentum peccatis reos per naturam filios non teneri.
pass_a_gloss: It is therefore in the absolute, if Moses is believed more, through whom God speaks, than Augustine, through whom the Manichaean speaks, that sons are not held defendants by nature for parents' sins.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: It is therefore settled—if Moses, through whom God speaks, is believed rather than Augustine, through whom Mani speaks—that children are not made guilty by nature for their parents’ sins.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Continues the explicit argument from the law forbidding punishment of parents and children for one another’s sins.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
